best_parts: node gate_t4: names the wrong model (the word colic), says why it tempts, refutes with the course of the pain, and offers a sure_note plus an agency 'Show me why' route
node gate_ok: 'I am sure, skip the lesson' fast lane jumps straight to the ladder probe, the only true skip lane in the segment
node ladder_t_hida: names HIDA as the 'most accurate' reflex and separates accuracy from 'first', the reverse-error repair for TR2
flaws: node gate: only one wrong option (Biliary colic) plus the key, so the probe is a two-way guess and the stem's 'tender' and 'positive Murphy's sign' point straight at the key

node ladder_q: probes only 'first' test; the TR2 'most sensitive and specific' form is never offered as a choice, so the learner who thinks ultrasound answers every gallbladder question is not diagnosed
node gate_t4 retry: 'Try again' returns to the identical probe with the identical options, so the trap is not re-tested in another form within the segment
node ladder_explain: teaches HIDA as most sensitive before the learner has committed to it; no probe commits to that idea

best_parts: node sens: asks 'most sensitive and specific' after the first-test probe, so the learner must switch from 'first' to 'accurate' before any HIDA explanation; the Ultrasound option is the TR2 trap in its exact form
node sens_t2: names the wrong model ('ultrasound is the test you order first, so it feels like the answer to everything'), refutes it with the first-versus-accurate wording, and has a sure_note
node pain_t4 and pain_tp: two different wrong pain descriptions (waves every few minutes, and pain only after meals) each name their tempting clue and refute it from the course of the pain
node case: commit-first probe with a stem that ends 'Commit before you read on', then the TR4 and choledocholithiasis partial traps offered as a real choice set
flaws: no fast lane anywhere in the segment; an expert who answers case and first_test correctly must still read contrast, boundary and pain
node contrast: a full explanation of colic versus cholecystitis comes before the pain probe, so the pain criteria are told before they are asked
node pain: the distractor 'Pain only after meals, never radiating' uses the absolute word 'never' and is the weakest option, so it is easy to eliminate by form
node sens_t2 retry: returns to the same probe with the same options; the TR2 trap is re-tested only later in another segment

best_parts: node case_t4 and show_colic: wrong-model feedback for colic followed by a clean explanation of the course of pain, with an agency route
node scan_t2: names the tempting 'feels thorough' model and refutes it with the first-test wording
node acc_t2: the most-accurate probe catches the first-versus-accurate confusion with its own sure_note
flaws: node ladder: explains that HIDA is the most sensitive and specific test before the acc probe asks the same question, so the acc probe is recognition after telling, not a commitment
nodes scan and acc: each probe has a single wrong option (CT, or Ultrasound), so the learner's choice separates little beyond a binary guess
no pain-character probe and no second TR4 form, so the colic trap is tested once
no fast lane and no hint-ladder branch beyond a single hint per probe; all learners take the same path

merge_ideas: b's four-probe order (case, pain, first_test, sens) with a's skip lane: a sure answer at case_ok or sens offers 'skip the lesson' straight to the next probe
b's sens probe with a's ladder_t_hida reverse-error wording as the feedback for a learner who picks HIDA for 'first'
b's ordering (commit, then tell, then the next probe) with c's acc_t2 sure_note, placed on the TR2 probe
a's gate stem with only the colic trap removed of its surface clues, so the stem holds the diagnosis but not the answer shape, and a third wrong option taken from b's case set
